2025_100_m061725bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held June 17, 2025 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, called to order by President Philippart at 7:02 p.m. before an audience of approximately 150. The meeting opened with a public hearing on the proposed 2025/2026 budget presented by Mr. Trudel, and closed with President Philippart's announcement that the Board had completed Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky's performance evaluation, again rated him a highly effective leader, and would extend his contract for another three years. The Board also adopted a Resolution in Support of Gun Safety and Safe Gun Storage 7-0 and approved elementary writing units of study on a divided 5-2 vote.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, June 17, 2025, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Called to order by President Philippart at 7:02 p.m.; adjourned at 8:58 p.m. Approximately 150 members of the audience attended.

**Attendance**
Present: Dr. Philippart plus Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler. Also present: Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Pagel, Griffor, Haezebrouck, Recker, Detmer, Singh, Cross, and Trudel.

**Public Hearing - 2025/2026 Proposed Budget**
Mr. Trudel presented the proposed budget to the Board and community with a PowerPoint, noting the budget had been reviewed in detail with the Board at the June workshop. He covered tax values, homestead/non-homestead millage, general fund adjustments and assumptions, ancillary funds, the sinking fund and capital projects fund, student enrollment, foundation allowance history, and revenues and expenditures. The Board indicated it had reviewed the proposed budget in its entirety at the June 3rd Workshop. One community member asked for clarification on what sinking funds are and how they are used.

**Recognitions**
- TSD Mission Moment: Ava Bunao, Athens High School graduate, runner up for the 2025 Gold Award Girl Scout Young Women of Distinction for her project "On the Spot Community First Aid Awareness for Outdoor Recreation," and recipient of the GSUSA Gold Award Scholarship given to one Gold Award Girl Scout per council. She will attend Michigan State University as a biochemistry major.
- TSD Mission Moment: the Bemis Math Pentathlon team, winners of the 2025 National Math Pentathlon First Place Gold Trophy, introduced by Bemis Principal Mrs. Harleen Singh.
- Student Spotlight: TSD Creative Guild graduates Akshaya Rachamadugu (2025 Troy High) and Anoush Rophael (2025 Athens), presented by Mr. Thomas Butcher.

**Resolution in Support of Gun Safety and Safe Gun Storage**
Moved by Mrs. Zendler, supported by Mrs. Anne. Whereas clauses cite that firearm-related deaths are the leading cause of death among children and adolescents; that firearm death rates among ages 14 to 17 are 22.5% higher than motor vehicle-related death rates; that 76% of school-grounds attackers acquired a firearm from the home of a parent or close relative per a US Secret Service report; that roughly 350 children under 18 unintentionally shoot themselves or someone else each year; that nearly 22,000 Americans die by firearm suicide annually including over 950 children and teens; and that 47% of firearm owners with children at home do not safely store at least one weapon. The resolution directs the Superintendent to communicate the importance of safe firearm storage during gun violence awareness month and to include secure-storage material in annual notification materials. Adopted Yes 7, No 0, certified by Secretary Emina Alic under the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.

**Action Items**

| Item | Mover / Support | Vote |
|---|---|---|
| Consent agenda items A through K | Haupt / Alic | 7-0 |
| Ms. Ebert, Assistant Principal, Baker Middle School | Alic / Haupt | 7-0 |
| Dr. David Recker, Director, Teaching & Learning | Anne / Potts | 7-0 |
| Ms. Reba McNally, Principal, Hamilton Elementary School | Alic / Anne | 7-0 |
| Elementary Writing Units of Study, grades K-5 | Potts / Alic | 5-2 |
| Smith Middle School EPIC system, VSC Inc., $173,978.00 | Alic / Anne | 7-0 |

Each administrative appointment is a two-year administrative contract without tenure commencing with the 2025-26 school year. On the writing curriculum, Mrs. Zendler and Dr. Melton stated they would vote no; Mrs. Anne shared sentiments but supported adoption. Yes: Alic, Anne, Haupt, Philippart, Potts. No: Melton, Zendler.

**Other**
Ten community members addressed the Board during non-agenda public communication; no action was taken. Dr. Philippart reported the Board completed Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky's evaluation, again rated him a highly effective leader, and will extend his contract for another three years. Board members offered end-of-year sentiments and an OCSBA update on pending legislation and budgets. Next regular meeting announced for July 15th at 9:30 a.m. at the Administration Building; the August 19th meeting also at the Administration Building at 6:00 p.m.

**Meeting identification.** Minutes of a regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held June 17, 2025 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. In addition to Dr. Philippart, Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Pagel, Griffor, Haezebrouck, Recker, Detmer, Singh, Cross, and Trudel. Approximately 150 members of the audience attended. The meeting adjourned at 8:58 p.m. The minutes are submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, and carry the typist notation EA/jh.

**Public hearing on the 2025/2026 proposed budget.** The business portion opened with a public hearing on the proposed 2025/2026 budget. Mr. Trudel presented the details of the proposed budget to the Board and community and shared a PowerPoint presentation. He noted the proposed budget had been reviewed in great detail with the Board at the June workshop. His presentation addressed tax values, homestead and non-homestead millage, general fund adjustments and assumptions, ancillary funds, the sinking fund, and the capital projects fund. He also reviewed student enrollment, the District's foundation allowance history, and revenues and expenditures. The Board indicated it had reviewed the proposed budget in its entirety at the June 3rd Workshop. President Philippart invited questions from the audience related to the proposed budget; one question was asked by a community member to clarify what the sinking funds are and how they are used.

**Recognition: Ava Bunao.** The Board recognized recent graduate Ava Bunao, named a runner up for the 2025 Gold Award Girl Scout Young Women of Distinction for her project "On the Spot Community First Aid Awareness for Outdoor Recreation." The project focused on providing access to first aid resources in local outdoor recreation areas and on teaching community members how to use them. It also earned the GSUSA Gold Award Scholarship, which is awarded to one Gold Award Girl Scout per council. Ava graduated from Athens High School with high honors and numerous scholarships and will begin college at Michigan State University as a biochemistry major and a student in the Osteopathic Medical Scholars Program on a pre-medicine track. She was invited to the podium to describe her Gold Award project.

**Recognition: Bemis Math Pentathlon team.** A second Mission Moment honored the Bemis Math Pentathlon team for earning the 2025 National Math Pentathlon First Place Gold Trophy. Mrs. Harleen Singh, Principal of Bemis, came to the podium to describe the achievement and introduce the champion team. The following students received a certificate of achievement and congratulations from Board members: Aashvi Vatsa, Aiden Rajbhandari, Anika Gollamudi, Aryian Majjhoo, Elias Roumayah, Ishan Vankadara, Shardul Joshi, Vihaan Palepu, Atharv Salimath, Ayona Chauhan, Bhashith Thulugu, Mannat Thakur, Navneeth Sheshathri, Ryka Kashi, Sanvika GopalaKrishnan, Sarah Farah, Vihaa Chethan, Alexander Majjhoo, Aniket Pagi, Ayla Majjhoo, Cali Hoskins, Charles Carlisle, Dhruhi Bhatt, Eleanor Roumayah, Feruz Mamarasulov, Gourika Kurkimatt, Grace Thomas, Irene Thommana, Naaga Nainika Dhavala, Nainika Chowdhury, Nate Zhang, Prarthana Gowda, Srihith Gattupalli, Varun Prasanth Kumar, Anushka Sonar, Asha Thabolingam, Bruno Redondo, Fatima Bilal, Hari Kern, Kaira Singh, Ritwika Thanigaivel, Saisha Fegade, Tiyasa Giri, Adam Majjhoo, Anirudh Ganesh, Isaac Thommana, Padmesh Lekkala Haribabu, Pugal Suresh Babu, Rayan Pedaballe, Shrivatsav Santapuri, Dheeya Gopalakrishnan, Satyapavana Gattupalli, Shilpa Manni, and Varnika Prasanth Kumar.

**Student Spotlight.** The Student Spotlight recognized creative achievement in the TSD Creative Guild, described at this meeting as more accurately an Alumni Spotlight. Recent graduates Akshaya Rachamadugu (2025 Troy High graduate) and Anoush Rophael (2025 Athens graduate) were recognized for dedication to Creative Guild throughout their high school careers. Mr. Thomas Butcher was invited up to share the achievement.

**Resolution in Support of Gun Safety and Safe Gun Storage.** Moved by Mrs. Zendler and supported by Mrs. Anne. The whereas clauses state that the safety and well-being of students, teachers, and staff is a top priority in the Troy School District; that firearm-related deaths are the leading cause of death among children and adolescents; that rates of death from firearms among ages 14 to 17 are now 22.5% higher than motor vehicle-related death rates, and that in the U.S. middle and high school age children are now more likely to die as the result of a firearm injury than from any other single cause of death; that according to a report from the US Secret Service, in incidents of gun violence on school grounds 76% of attackers acquired a firearm from the home of a parent or another close relative; that every year roughly 350 children under the age of 18 unintentionally shoot themselves or someone else; that nearly 22,000 Americans die by firearm suicide every year, including over 950 children and teens; that research indicates 47% of firearm owners who have children living in their homes do not safely store at least one of their weapons; that evidence strongly suggests secure firearm storage is an essential component of any effective community safety strategy; that keeping students, teachers and staff safe from the threat of gun violence should be the responsibility of all adult stakeholders in the district; and that preventative measures require action now.

The resolving clauses direct the Superintendent to periodically communicate the importance of safe firearm storage and other firearm safety and violence prevention measures during gun violence awareness month, and to disseminate material on an annual basis stressing the importance of secure storage of firearms by including it in the District's annual notification materials. A further clause commits the Board and Superintendent to continue working with local law enforcement agencies, medical and mental health agencies, and non-profit organizations to increase efforts to inform District parents of their obligations regarding secure storage of firearms in their homes and other gun violence prevention safety measures. A final clause provides that the resolution shall not be construed to conflict with any existing Michigan or federal law. The vote was Yes 7, No 0, and the resolution was declared adopted. Emina Alic, Secretary, Board of Education, certified the resolution as a true and complete copy duly adopted at a regular meeting held on the 17th day of June, 2025, with notice given in full compliance with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976. Citations appended to the resolution reference news.umich.edu, labblog.uofmhealth.org, the US Secret Service publication Protecting America's Schools, Everytown Research's "Not an Accident" map and its report on the rise of firearm suicide among young Americans, a Pew Research Center guns report, and David C. Grossman et al., "Gun Storage Practices and Risk of Youth Suicide and Unintentional Firearm Injuries," JAMA 293, no. 6 (2005): 707-14.

**Additions and deletions; agenda-item public communication.** None recorded for either.

**Consent agenda.** Moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Alic that the Troy Board of Education approve items A through K on the consent agenda: minutes of the May 6, 2025 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the May 20, 2025 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report for April 2025; Food Service Contract Renewal; Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) Membership Resolution 2025/2026; 2024/2025 Budget Amendment; 2025/2026 Budget Appropriations Resolution; District Pavement Crackfill & Striping; Troy Preschool Playground Pavillion Purchase/Installation; Schools of Choice 2025-26; and First Student Contract Renewal. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Personnel.** Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Board issue a two-year administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Ms. Ebert, who will begin her duties as Assistant Principal, Baker Middle School commencing with the 2025-26 school year. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mrs. Potts that the Board issue a two-year administrative contract without tenure to Dr. David Recker, who will begin his duties as Director, Teaching & Learning commencing with the 2025-26 school year. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Anne that the Board issue a two-year administrative contract without tenure to Ms. Reba McNally, who will begin her duties as Principal, Hamilton Elementary School commencing with the 2025-26 school year. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Curriculum: Elementary Writing Units of Study.** The Director of Teaching and Learning, with members of the Teaching & Learning team, provided information to Board members on recommended materials for grades K-5 for the upcoming school year; Board members had reviewed the plan and asked questions following the Board Workshop. Moved by Mrs. Potts and supported by Mrs. Alic that the recommended materials for grades K-5 be approved starting in the 2025-2026 school year. Mrs. Zendler shared a statement informing the community and fellow board members that she would be voting no on the proposed writing curriculum. Dr. Melton shared that upon further research and investigation she would not support the adoption. Mrs. Anne shared sentiments about the proposed writing curriculum but indicated she would support its adoption. Vote: Yes 5 (Alic, Anne, Haupt, Philippart, Potts), No 2 (Melton, Zendler).

**Business: Smith Middle School EPIC system.** Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Anne that the purchase of an EPIC system for Smith Middle School be approved through VSC Inc. in the amount of $173,978.00, and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Public communication (non-agenda) and other.** Ten community members addressed the Board during public communication; no action was taken by the Board. Under Other, no items were recorded, but Dr. Philippart shared a statement indicating that the Board recently completed Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky's performance evaluation and shared a brief assessment with the community: Dr. Machesky is once again a highly effective leader and the Board will be extending his contract for another three years. Board members shared sentiments about the end of the school year, congratulated graduates and retirees, wished the community a safe summer, and congratulated and welcomed the new administrators. An update on pending legislation and budgets from the recent OCSBA meeting was shared. Dr. Philippart announced the next regular Board meeting for July 15th at 9:30 a.m. at the Administration Building and the August 19th Board meeting also at the Administration Building at 6:00 p.m.

2025_101_m052025bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held May 20, 2025 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, with Vice President Anne presiding at 7:04 p.m. in place of absent President Philippart before an audience of approximately 200. **Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, May 20, 2025, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. **Attendance**
Present with Mrs. Anne: Board members Alic, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler, plus Superintendent Machesky and administrators including Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Detmer, Keyser, Brennan, Cottone, Barsh, Crowe, Haezebrouck, Smotherman, Burdette, Pagel, and Trudel.

**Recognitions**

| Resolution | Mover / Support | Vote |

| Mrs. Jesse Allgeier | Assistant Principal, Troy High School | July 1, 2025 | Alic / Haupt |
| Mrs. Jamie Evans | Special Education Supervisor, Services Building | July 1, 2025 | Potts / Zendler |

The Ivey, Allgeier, and Evans contracts are two-year probationary administrative contracts without tenure; the Burdette contract is a two-year administrative contract without tenure.

**Public Communication and Student Reports**
Nine community members addressed the Board; no action was taken. Student representatives Kristian Vitanovich (Troy College and Career High School), Nurayda Albeez (International Academy-East), and Adam McManus (Troy High School) reported on school activities; Diana D'Aloisio (Athens High School) was not in attendance.

**Meeting identification.** Minutes of a regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held May 20, 2025 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Vice President Anne presided for President Philippart, who was not in attendance, and called the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m. In addition to Mrs. Anne, Board members Alic, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Detmer, Keyser, Brennan, Cottone, Barsh, Crowe, Haezebrouck, Smotherman, Burdette, Jansen, Roncone, Brinks, House, Hall, Keen, Detmer, DiPonio, Harker, Pagel, and Trudel. Approximately 200 members of the audience attended. The meeting adjourned at 8:54 p.m. Minutes submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the typist notation EA/jh.

**Recognition: 2025 Outstanding Support Staff Award.** The Board recognized the District's Outstanding Support Person of the Year, a category covering bus drivers, secretaries, paraprofessionals, student support aides, custodial staff, food service, technology, childcare, security, and more. There were 24 nominees this year. The 2025 honoree is Phyllis Walters, Administrative Assistant to the Principal at Wass Elementary School, nominated by the entire Wass staff. Nomination comments read into the record described her as a problem-solver who heads off problems before they can become one; extremely organized, efficient, trustworthy, and kind; going above and beyond for students and families every day; the reason Wass runs smoothly and the backbone of the school; and resilient, adaptable, with unwavering dedication. Her name was engraved on the Support Person Plaque that will be displayed at her building for the next year, and she was surprised with a check for $250 from the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence. A short video of the surprise visit was shared with the Board and audience. Principal Kristin Crowe was present to accept the plaque on Phyllis Walters' behalf, as she was unable to attend the meeting.

**Recognition: Troy School District retirees.** The Board recognized employees who retired or expressed their intention to retire at the end of the 2024-2025 school year. Mr. Pagel read each name with the length of the employee's District career: Ruba Alexander (Teacher, Troy Union, dedicated employee since 1995), Nadia Barbat (Teacher, Baker, since 2005), Michelle Barsh (Principal, Martell, since 2018), Heather Childress (Teacher, Martell, since 1998), Kelly Chlebek (Counselor, Baker, since 2004), Cindy Christiansen (Teacher, Larson, since 2007), Melissa Curth (Assistant Principal, Troy High, since 1995), Paula Davidson (Para-Professional, Wattles, since 2010), Carol Dospil (Teacher, Hamilton, since 1985), Laura Duzey (Central Enrollment/Pupil Accounting Coordinator, Central Office, since 1999), Erin Fischer-Ballew (Teacher, Troy High, since 2000), Rose Gavrilovska (Systems Analyst, Services, since 2024), Shelley Hakala (Teacher, Troy High, since 1999), Joe Havrilla (Teacher, Boulan Park, since 1994), Jane Held (Teacher, Martell, since 2003), Robert Holder (Teacher, Athens, since 2000), Carrie Johnson (Teacher, Baker, since 1999), Patrick Koneval (Teacher, Smith, since 1991), Sandy Koneval (Teacher, Boulan Park, since 1993), Frank Leone (Teacher, Boulan Park, since 1981), Kathryn Loch (Teacher, Baker/Larson, since 2003), Diane Loucks (Teacher, Troy High, since 1995), Krista Manfredi (Teacher, Athens, since 1974), Benjamin Martin (Teacher, Wattles, since 2000), Cathy Matthes (Secretary, Barnard, since 1996), Shelley McHugh (Teacher, Larson, since 2002), Brenda Rice (Teacher, Athens, since 1996), Jennifer Sobczynski (Teacher, Troy High, since 1990), Linda Stanko (Early Childhood Coordinator, Preschool, since 1985), Jennifer Taylor (Teacher, Boulan Park, since 1986), Lori Ulewicz (Teacher, Baker, since 1989), Carolyn Van Noord (Project Search Instructor, Troy School District, since 2006), Marie Weber (Explorer Supervisor, Preschool, since 1999), and Mike DeSantis (Teacher, Athens, beloved employee since 1996).

**Recognition: Athens girls' powerlifting champions.** The Board celebrated the Troy Athens Powerlifting team as 2025 State Champions, noting the team secured its third consecutive state title while competing on national and global stages and shattering school, state, and national records. The following powerlifters came forward for a certificate and congratulations from the Board: Alessandra Alojipan, Julia Arnett, Lillian Flores, Mariana Gould, Sara Graunstadt, Mya Hangstebeck, Camilla Inadeski, Reemas Kaakarni, Lillian Kotila, Ciara Lenz, Indira Martinez, Cassidy Morse, Izzie Piotrowski, Addison Pokley, Erica Seidel, Kata Tasich, Luleta Thaqi, Mikayla Twum, and Emma Walters.

**Legislative CAP students report.** The Board welcomed students from the Legislative track of the District's Career Accelerator Program (CAP), who have been engaged in learning about levels of government from the school board and the city to state senators and representatives. Two students shared experiences, insights, and how CAP affected their educational journey. The students named were Aarav Akolkar (THS), Tanmayee Choudary Gudi (IAE), Jackson Kanczuzewski (AHS), Amarachi Obiakor (IAE), Melita Pereira (IAE), Naina Rodrigues (THS), Jyostsna Shivakumar (THS), Ragavarshini Venkatesh (THS), and Vinicius Zanta Leao da Silva (IAE).

**National Teacher Appreciation Week resolution.** Teacher Appreciation Week is observed nationally each May and was celebrated Monday, May 5th through Friday, May 9th this year. Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt, the resolution recites that teachers inspire, nurture and open children's minds to new ideas; that teachers promote and strengthen the principles of democratic equality, develop leaders and encourage critical thinking; that Troy teachers set the bar for excellence in education and continually exceed the highest standards in the profession; and that the goal of Teacher Appreciation Week is to raise national and local awareness of teaching excellence in building a better society. It resolves that the Troy School District supports National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 5-9, 2025 and encourages schools and community to recognize the vital and changing role of teachers. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

**Mental Health Awareness Month resolution.** Each year Oakland Community Health Network and its service provider network host initiatives promoting community awareness about mental illness, and school boards across Oakland County were asked to recognize May as Mental Health Awareness Month. Moved by Dr. Melton and supported by Mrs. Potts, the resolution recites that mental health is important for individual well-being and vitality as well as that of families, communities, and schools; that one in five of all Americans, including children, experience mental health issues that could lead to school difficulties, physical problems, and even suicide; and that May 8, 2025 is designated National Children's Mental Health Awareness Day and May 12 through May 18, 2025 is designated Children's Mental Health Acceptance Week. It resolves that the Troy Board of Education recognizes May 2025 as Mental Health Awareness Month and seeks to increase awareness and understanding of mental illness and the need to support all people seeking help. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

**Additions and deletions; agenda-item public communication.** None recorded for either.

**Consent agenda.** Moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Alic that the Troy Board of Education approve items A through K on the consent agenda: minutes of the April 1, 2025 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the April 22, 2025 Special Board Meeting & Closed Session; minutes of the April 22, 2025 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report for March 2025; Approve Oakland Intermediate School District Budget; Resolution to Hold a Public Hearing on the Proposed 2025/2026 School Year Budget; IA Budget Approval for the 2024/2025 School Year; OCSBA Amendment to Bylaws; Troy High Kitchen Upgrades; Transportation Parking Lot Lighting; and Beverage Cooler Replacement at Baker MS. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

**Personnel.** Moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Zendler that the Board issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Colette Ivey, who will begin her duties as Principal, Martell Elementary School effective July 1, 2025. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart. Moved by Dr. Melton and supported by Mrs. Potts that the Board issue a two-year administrative contract without tenure to Mr. Ross Burdette, who will begin his duties as Principal, Hill Elementary School commencing with the 2025-26 school year. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart. Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Board issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mrs. Jesse Allgeier, who will begin her duties as Assistant Principal, Troy High School effective July 1, 2025. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart. Moved by Mrs. Potts and supported by Mrs. Zendler that the Board issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mrs. Jamie Evans, who will begin her duties as Special Education Supervisor, Services Building effective July 1, 2025. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

**Curriculum and Business.** No items were presented under either heading.

**Public communication and student representative reports.** Nine community members addressed the Board during public communication; no action was taken by the Board. Kristian Vitanovich, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, reported on events and activities at his school. Nurayda Albeez, student representative for International Academy-East, reported on events and activities at her school. Adam McManus, student representative for Troy High School, reported on events and activities at his school. Diana D'Aloisio, student representative for Athens High School, was not in attendance.

**Board member comments and sentiments.** Mrs. Alic shared sentiments about Boulan Park 8th grade student Bilal Ahmad, who passed away unexpectedly during Freshman Orientation at Troy High School on May 1st, and noted the family would hold a Celebration of Life to honor him. Other comments congratulated the retirees again; expressed appreciation for public comments regarding the writing curriculum; invited attendance at the June 3rd Workshop for information on PA146 legislation; thanked teachers for another great school year; gave a shout out to 2025 graduates, with ceremonies for THS and AHS on 5/31, IA on 6/1, and TCCHS on 6/4; announced the upcoming SSAB Leadership Conference 5/23, Open Air Fest 5/28, and TFEE Golf Outing 6/10; welcomed new administrators; and thanked all who helped with 8th Grade Interviews. Mrs. Anne announced the next Board Workshop for Tuesday, June 3rd at 6:00 p.m. at the Services Building and the next Board of Education Meeting for Tuesday, June 17th at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building.
